title.narrative: Increasing income and employment opportunities in agro-industry value chains
Ökade inkomst- och sysselsättningsmöjligheter inom agroindustrins värdekedjor

description.narrative: Det övergripande målet är att stödja utvecklingen av inkluderande och hållbara marknadssystem i utvalda värdekedjor som effektivt kopplar småskaliga jordbrukare och jordbruksbaserade mikro-, små och medelstora företag (MSME) till inhemska, regionala och /eller globala marknader genom klustersamarbete och i syfte att främja lokal förädling. Programmet från denna förstudie förväntas bidra till Liberias ekonomiska diversifiering, gröna tillväxt, samt fattigdomsbekämpning genom att generera ökade inkomster och anständig sysselsättning (Decent Work), särskilt för kvinnor och unga.

The overall objective is to facilitate the development of inclusive and sustainable market systems in selected value chains, which effectively link smallholder farmers and agriculture-based Micro, Small and Medium sized Enterprises (MSMEs) to domestic, regional and /or global markets through clustering and with the aim to foster local value addition. The programme emanating from this PA is expected to contribute to Liberia’s economic diversification, green growth as well as poverty alleviation by generating income and decent employment, in particular for women and youth.

The project constitutes the PA phase of a new programme planned by the Embassy of Sweden in the context of its cooperation with Liberia. The overall objective is to facilitate the development of inclusive and sustainable market systems in selected value chains, which effectively link smallholder farmers and agriculture-based Micro, Small and Medium sized Enterprises (MSMEs) to domestic, regional and /or global markets through clustering and with the aim to foster local value addition. The envisaged full programme emanating from this inception is expected to contribute to Liberias economic diversification, green growth as well as poverty alleviation by generating income and decent employment, in particular for women and youth.

The PA have the following expected Outcomes: (a) Programme document prepared and validated in a participatory manner, and (b) Consolidation of results from GROW Liberia activities in the cocoa and vegetables value chains (VCs).
Based on the reporting, follow-up including the engagement in the field, it is concluded that the project has been progressing well and according to plan during the main part of the Inception Phase, particularly in the area of cocoa which have clearly delivered beneficiary impact and been able to accelerate the work that was previously done by Adam Smith International during GROW 1. UNIDO have by bringing their own expertise and knowledge effectively consolidated the work with a large number and range of partners, while maintaining and developing the trust and brand that GROW 1 had created during almost nine years.
During the period from start to end of the inception support, UNIDO have established a national project office. Following advertisement of local vacancies, a UNIDO panel selected two senior and two field experts for cocoa and vegetables value chains. Three of them have experience of working under GROW 1 and have significant experience and networks in the cocoa and vegetable value chains. They are also supported by two national project assistants who provide various administrative support to ensure the effective and efficient running of project events, missions and workshops. The staff have been trained on UNIDO procedures for procurement, travel, ethical behavior, etc. This training included training on Market System Development (MSD) for the project team. Upon invitation from UNIDO, the training was also attended by three officers from Mercy Corps employed under the PROSPECTS IV project to provide alignment and synergies.
UNIDO have also performed diagnostic analyses to collect field-level information and data in the cocoa and vegetables value chains (named horticulture under GROW 2 to integrate fruits), and shortlisted new value chains with potential for market systems development as per the requirement by the Embassy. UNIDO international experts travelled to Liberia to on several field missions to, among other things, map and engage key stakeholders, policy makers, business support organizations, training and extension institutions and industry players (e.g., exporters and importers) for cocoa and vegetable value chains, but also for the agriculture sector in general. They also prepared robust value chains workplans for the GROW 2 project proposal and finalized geographic areas based on value chain selection and target groups.
Certain challenges among the cooperatives and producer groups were evident from the scoping missions; including weak governance structures as depicted in the poor or complete lack of documented business history, no financial statements; rudimentary processing setups with implications for meeting food safety and quality standards. In cocoa, there are additionally issues of side selling by farmers that makes investments in the sector by exporters a very high risk proposition; a policy and regulatory framework that may be concentrating opportunities for a limited set of players especially for exporting cocoa; poor road infrastructure and networks that imposes additional costs for all supply chain actors; and challenges with accessing finance by exporters, licensed buying companies, aggregators and cooperatives which creates an overreliance on trade partners. In vegetables, smallholder farmers have not been adequately integrated into a viable value chain system and productivity is low due to limited access to improved and certified seeds and fertilizers as well as poor agronomic practices.
The proposed GROW 2 project will focus its activities on Nimba, Lofa and Bong Counties, where cocoa production is concentrated (and also to provide some synergies from LSFRP3 improved feeder roads and ongoing construction of Village Access Roads). Within the spirit of fostering diversification of production (and hence income), work in the other two value chains (cassava and horticulture) will also primarily focus on these three Counties. The programme remains open to work in other counties as there may be additional opportunities in line with the programme objectives and flexible management approach.
Following the analyses, UNIDO organized a validation workshop with key stakeholders to use their market knowledge and sector expertise to select the value chains and get buy-in from key stakeholders on the systemic change vision. Ministry of Agriculture participated in this workshop together with the Embassy and other important stakeholders. The workshop confirmed the relevance of continuing engagement in cocoa and horticulture VC. The cassava VC was also added, given (i) its key contribution to food security (it being the second most consumed crop in Liberia), (ii) the potential for growth in supply (its current production not satisfying local demand) and also (iii) the scope for value addition, covering several products among which gari (including potential for its nutritional fortification), cassava flour, cassava chips, starch, and animal feed. The Government of Liberia has also prioritized cassava in its five-year National Development Plan referred to as the Pro-Poor Agenda for Prosperity and Development (PAPD) 2018-2023. During the workshop the rice value chain was also identified as a priority value chain related to food security objectives, however this value chain is not retained under GROW 2 proposal as a separate focus area. This is primarily based on the low potential for value addition in this sector and taking into consideration the large number of projects in this field.
In addition to the validation workshop, UNIDO have had numerous consultations with implementing agencies of related support programmes.
The project has also participated in an international cluster conference held in Ghana to foster and strengthen linkages with experiences and expertise in the region. To foster and strengthen linkages with experiences and expertise in the region, the project organized a study visit to Ghana of the national cocoa expert and two Government of Liberia representatives (Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Commerce and Industry) in June 2022. The delegation visited four producers in Ghana; a women cooperative producing cassava, a greenhouse producing vegetables, a company processing and packaging vegetables, fruits and herbs, and a company producing, processing and exporting cocoa products. The study visit ultimately initiated discussions on knowledge exchanges in the region, focusing on replicating Ghana's success in agro-processing.
Regarding the consolidation of results from GROW Liberia activities in the cocoa and vegetables value chains (VCs), it was observed that consolidation of activities for organic certification is most urgent and UNIDO has worked extensively with stakeholders in Liberia to continue preparations for their certification. Several cocoa partners are in the process for Organic certification with one already completed and more to be completed by October. Partners are also in the process to receive Fair Trade certification. UNIDO have also conducted training of national experts in Organic, Fairtrade and Rainforest Alliance Certifications, as there are no national certification experts in Liberia. The project also developed a workplan on identifying and characterizing the Liberia Flavor Profile for cocoa. For vegetables. UNIDO have started sensitization and awareness creation on organic vegetables production as one of several activities.
The project has submitted a final project proposal in time according to the Agreement. The proposal is capitalizing on the results and lessons of the Adam Smith International implemented GROW 1, and the analyses from the inception phase.
The project team, both the country team and the international experts in Vienna, have during the period been transparent, responsive and focused on results while including the Embassy in its work and progress. UNIDO have also been observant on suggestions from the Embassy.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
